reason: Lens: schedule and feasibility. As described, the idea has about a 0.15-0.3 chance of a scored LB probe by 29 Sep 10:00 UTC, below the 0.7 bar. Its lab step depends on idea 1's x138 train cache, and that cache cannot validate the p_edge part honestly anyway. (1) Dependency. The 42 h path runs 'after idea 1's lab' on 'idea 1's x138 cache with the edge dump on'. Idea 1 (divins-x138-lab-retune) has been refuted by both sibling verdicts: value gives public +0.000, and schedule gives P(scored) ~0.2 and puts the x138 run on 199 train videos at 13-16 GPU-h, with a REPAIR_DEADLINE_S guard problem and no x138 train harness (v_divisions_divins-x138-lab-retune_schedule.json). If idea 1 is dropped, this idea would carry the full 13-16 GPU-h, about half of vitalii's weekly 30 GPU-h, plus about 8-10 h of harness work. That buys a lab gate that the idea itself calls 'sanity check only', discounted by 50-100%, because the SimpleNodeTransformer was trained on all 199 train videos (BRIEF lab caveat: edge filter lab +0.016 -> LB 0). No honest offline validation of p_edge exists before the deadline: that would need an edge-network retrain by embryo, which takes days. (2) The dump switch must be set BEFORE the train run starts (26 Sep ~00:05 in the sibling plan, or on friend A's 5070 Ti). Friend A has made no commits since 24 Sep 04:12 MSK and is waiting for #34 (CONTEXT 25 Sep 10:20 block). The dump code path has never run: BIOHUB_CACHE_EDGE_THRESHOLD is 1.0 in x138, and no kernel in the repo sets it lower. (3) Implementation as described partly holds. The anchor exists at runtime: the dump patch sits in the same try block as the LOWDET patch, which works (1,337 readmitted nodes on the dummy run). The runtime and disk cost is small: one np.nonzero per frame pair plus an npz that is already written. Two things differ from what the idea assumes. First, the dumped prob is the dual-seed-blended SOFTMAX over sources for each target (tools/repo/scripts/predict_unet_transformer.py l.74 and l.457-458; x138 does not override edge_activation). So p(u->v) means 'u is v's parent rather than another source', not an independent link probability. For an orphan v (the default insertion branch), the mass tends to fall on the nearest source, often u, so beta mostly acts on the steal branch. Second, node ids come from build_graph's bulk_add_nodes in coords order (l.116-145). The id mapping through the ILP, readmit and gap fill needs a positional assert that only a GPU dummy run can check. (4) Calendar arithmetic (GUESSES). P(#34/#35 green-light the x138 + insertion base) ~0.7. P(idea 1's cache is actually launched with the dump on and finishes by 27 Sep 12:00) ~0.4-0.5. P(loader, mapping and grid work first time) ~0.85. P(the in-sample sanity gate passes) ~0.5-0.6. Product: about 0.12-0.18, and 0.25-0.3 with no gate. (5) Even when scored, the probe cannot decide. The expected effect of +0.000..+0.002 and the idea's own ceiling of +0.007 over about 8 evaluable public forks sit at or below the LB noise (~0.003, BRIEF). Its adoption rule 'a tie is acceptable' therefore adopts on noise. Cited numbers check out: B20 16/319/135 (CONTEXT l.1011-1013); 15 of 43 FP forks have the ILP child wrong and the added child right (wf_ideas_v2/r1_research_fork-midpoint-filter.json); ILP forks 24/103 vs heuristic 23/172 (CONTEXT l.684, exp12, pre-official-metric); 12 insertions / 5 steals on the dummy (CONTEXT 25 Sep).
fix_if_any: Decouple it from idea 1 and ship it only as a blind, conservative rider on a probe that is already going out. The single config should only remove or re-target existing insertions, never add any. (a) Knobs in tools/div_insert.py, all exact no-ops at their defaults with byte-parity tests against the exp57b dummy outputs (scratchpad cmp57): edge_beta (0), edge_p_min (0), and steal_edge_margin (off). With steal_edge_margin on, the rule 'steal from any 0.0 edge' becomes 'steal only if p_dump(u,v) > p_dump(w,v) + margin'. This uses the real dumped prob instead of the 0.0 that the relink stores for pairs the ILP did not select (x138 cell 5 filter_output_graph: learned_edge_probs come only from ILP edges). (b) Loader in the divinsert glue: read /kaggle/working/edge_cache/{name}.npz and key by node id. Assert that npz coords[i] equals the geff node i's (t,z,y,x) before the tail. If the hit rate on non-readmit nodes is below 99%, fall back to beta 0 for that video and log it, so a mapping bug degrades to exp57b instead of corrupting output. Readmit and gap-fill nodes get p = 0 (u or v with p = 0 is skipped only when edge_p_min > 0). (c) Choose ONE blind setting: steal_edge_margin 0.2, edge_beta 0.5, edge_p_min 0. Do not use p_edge_min 0.2/0.4 blind, because the softmax semantics make orphan-v probs uninformative. (d) Launch only if #35 >= #34 - 0.003; otherwise there is no insertion to modulate. (e) Do not spend 13-16 GPU-h on a train cache for this idea. If idea 1's cache runs anyway, turn on BIOHUB_CACHE_EDGE_THRESHOLD=0.05 in it (a free rider), and use the result only to count how many insertions change, not as evidence of gain. (f) Treat the LB result as a sign check. Adopt only if LB >= best x138 + 0.002. On a tie, keep exp57b, because the change cannot be resolved within the noise.
realistic_public_gain: +0.000 (range -0.002..+0.002) over probe 35's config; below the ~0.003 LB noise. At most about 12 insertions (5 steals) per 4 dummy clips can change, and the public embryo has about 8 evaluable forks.
realistic_private_gain: +0.000..+0.001, sign uncertain. The edge network is in-sample on train and its softmax calibration on unseen embryos is unknown.
